turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on back, have a seat. I'll grab vitals before Dr. Shah comes in. Is that your partner in the blue jacket out front?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, that's Marcus. He can wait outside. I'm, um, pretty wound up about this.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Arm out for me. Blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy-four. Pulse is ninety-two.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature thirty-seven point one, oxygen sat ninety-nine percent, respirations sixteen. He'll be right in.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hey, sorry, this login keeps spinning. I'm Dr. Shah. What brought you in?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Spotting, and cramps. I'm pregnant, maybe eight to ten weeks. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Spotting — hold on, the screen just froze. How much bleeding, say that again?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It's light. Brown, sometimes pink on the tissue. Not like a real period. It started—
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did it start? I was clicking around, I missed the first part.
[SEG0010] person_1 (NURSE): I'll be at the desk. Just call if you want Marcus.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): About three days, maybe four. I don't know exactly, doctor.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Where are the cramps, and how bad?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Low in the pelvis, both sides. Dull, like a period, they come and go. Not the worst—
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any clots? Soaking a pad?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No clots. I haven't soaked a pad. Just the spotting.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, shoulder pain, or feeling like you'll pass out?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. No shoulder pain. I was lightheaded for a minute yesterday, then it went away.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nausea, vomiting, burning when you pee?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): A little queasy in the mornings. No vomiting. Pee is normal, no burning.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): When was your last period?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): The last period was around Diwali, or after. I don't know, doctor. I can't pin a date.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nothing exact in the chart either. Are your cycles regular?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really. Sometimes a month, sometimes I skip. I really don't know.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you do a home pregnancy test?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Two of them, both positive, last week. I was happy, and then this, and now I can't sleep, I just keep—
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Worrying, yeah. Is this your first pregnancy? Any miscarriages, any surgeries?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): First one. No miscarriages, no surgeries. Nothing like that.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): For medicines I'm on a prenatal, and last night I also—
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hang on, this field didn't save. Medicines again, slowly?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Prenatal vitamin, one tablet every morning. I don't know the brand, the bottle's pink. And ibuprofen two hundred milligrams, one tablet, for the cramp, then I stopped.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good that you stopped. No more ibuprofen while you're pregnant. If the cramps get bad you can use acetaminophen, six hundred fifty milligrams by mouth, every six hours as needed.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Allergies to any medicines?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe penicillin? My mom said that once. I never remember a reaction.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): So penicillin is a maybe. We'll come back to it. Do you smoke or drink?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. I had one glass of wine before I knew, about three weeks ago. Nothing since.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me check your belly. It's soft, mild tenderness low in the pelvis, no rebound.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that bad? I don't know, doctor, am I losing the pregnancy?
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): I can't tell from this. My working impression is threatened miscarriage versus just benign early spotting. The ultrasound has to sort it out.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm sending you for a transvaginal ultrasound today, plus bloodwork today, a quantitative hCG and a blood type with antibody screen.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Today, like before I go home?
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, both are happening before you leave. If the spotting hasn't settled in two weeks, we might repeat the ultrasound.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it gets worse tonight?
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): If you soak a pad in an hour, the pain turns severe, or you feel faint, go to the ER right away. Don't wait on a callback.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back here in two weeks regardless.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Can Marcus come in? I want him to hear the warning signs.
[SEG0046] person_1 (NURSE): I'll grab him.
[SEG0047] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hey. Sorry, the waiting room TV was loud. She's been spotting closer to a week, since around last Saturday.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): No, that's not right. It was three days, maybe four. I don't know, you're mixing it up with the queasy mornings.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): So three or four days from you, about a week from him. I'll chart the spotting as roughly three days to a week.
[SEG0050] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Also, allergies — she got hives from amoxicillin in college. She always blanks on it.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't remember that. I don't know, doctor. I only ever heard penicillin from my mom.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll flag a possible amoxicillin allergy with hives, not confirmed, and we won't use that drug family today.
[SEG0053] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She does take the prenatal every single morning. I watch her. The ibuprofen really was just that one pill.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Noted. Marcus, same rules — a pad an hour, severe pain, or fainting means the ER. Otherwise we're back in two weeks.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): What if the scan looks bad? I don't even know if I can—
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll talk the minute we have it. I'm not guessing off a frozen computer screen. Can you repeat the blood pressure? I never actually heard it.
[SEG0057] person_1 (NURSE): One eighteen over seventy-four, pulse ninety-two. I'll draw the labs and walk her over to ultrasound.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. I'm still scared.
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's understandable. Ultrasound and labs today, my office in two weeks, and the ER only if those warning signs show up.
[SEG0060] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll go straight there if we have to. Thanks.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): I still don't know my dates. I'm sorry.
[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): Don't apologize. The scan will date the pregnancy better than a guess around Diwali.
